title: HMAC: SETKEY claims key (returns 0) but Update may fall back — software HMAC uninitialized
description: Trigger: HmacSetKey with key <= 128B (SETKEY callback returns 0, wolfSSL skips its own ipad/opad key schedule). Then first HmacUpdate with a single call > 64KB (dataSz==0 && need > HMAC_MAX_BUF → returns CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE). wolfSSL falls back to its software HmacUpdate, but the software Hmac struct was never initialized (SETKEY returned 0). Bad behavior: wolfSSL computes HMAC with zero/garbage key material (depending on Hmac struct initialization) and returns it as success — silent wrong MAC. Contrast with AES SETKEY which deliberately returns CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE to keep the software schedule valid. Fix: either (a) make HMAC SETKEY also return CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE so wolfSSL keeps a valid software key schedule, or (b) never return CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE from Update after SETKEY claimed the key (i.e., if oversized, return WC_HW_E instead).
notes: CONFIRMED via wolfssl/wolfcrypt/src/hmac.c lines 549-558. wc_HmacSetKey_ex calls the SETKEY callback; if it returns anything other than CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE, it returns immediately (line 557) — BEFORE the software ipad/opad key schedule runs. If our SETKEY returns 0, wolfSSL skips the software key schedule entirely. If wc_HmacUpdate's callback then returns CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE (oversized first chunk), wolfSSL falls through to software HmacUpdate on zero-initialized (never-keyed) HMAC state. Result: HMAC computed with all-zeros ipad/opad, silently wrong.
